text:
maya: Quick check — onboarding mpt-x0 (70B) for serving. We have weights at s3://rwd-models/mpt-x0/70b/v1/weights.ckpt and tokenizer at s3://rwd-models/mpt-x0/tokenizer/tokenizer.json. Planning AWQ calibs + FP8 baseline. Need sign-off on: weights checksum, tokenizer quirks, config validation, calibration dataset, accuracy tradeoffs. @aj @liam can you take a look?

aj: I'll take a look in a bit. Quick heads-up: tokenizer is split-BPE with a custom BOS token mapping (BOS=1). There's a known mismatch vs HF tokenizers that affects leading whitespace. Use the tokenizer.json you linked rather than the HF-converted artifact.

maya: sample tokenization for the prompt "
/prompt Hello
":
```
"/prompt Hello" -> [2, 154, 908, 21, 5]  // illustrative
```
This reproduces what we see in the model checkpoints.

aj: Cool. Also saw model_config.json has max_seq_len: 4096 but our serving runtime currently enforces max_input=2048 per request to avoid OOMs on current pools. Can you set max_input=2048 in serve_config and add a config comment? Small PR will do.

liam: Note on FP8: prod-gpu-stable has FP8 kernels disabled for safety right now. FP8 smoke should run on dedicated QA infra only. For production, AWQ (4-bit) is safer and supported on current fleet. We can keep FP8 as an experimental artifact behind a flag.

quant-ops-bot: AUTO-CHECK RESULTS:
- weights checksum: OK (sha256: abc123def4567890...)
- tokenizer schema: VALID
- calib manifest: found at s3://rwd-calib/mpt-x0/2026-03-15/manifest.json
- missing: eval results link (required for approval)

sofia: From product/evals POV: previous AWQ configs saw ~1.5-2% drop on MMLU vs fp16 in some workloads. What's the expected delta here? Product preference is <=2% for this use-case. Also link evaluation suite (MMLU/T0-small/PIQA) when you have numbers.

maya: Running evals now on the AWQ quantized artifact vs fp16 baseline. Also pinging @aj for PR review: github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/432

aj: Reviewing PR #432. Left a couple of nits (docstring + one lint). The big flag: we added kv-cache preallocation toggle — that can increase mem footprint and reduce batch size. Recommend setting default batch size to 2 in serve_config until we verify memory footprint on canary.

infra: I ran accessibility and permission checks. Weights path accessible from dedicated fleet nodes. Added a temporary firewall rule for QA run. Infra run URL: https://infra.redwood/runs/775 (internal)

maya: Eval numbers (completed):
- MMLU avg: fp16 = 76.1, awq = 74.7 (delta -1.4%)
- T0-small: fp16 = 45.2, awq = 44.1 (delta -1.1%)
- PIQA: fp16 = 83.5, awq = 82.0 (delta -1.5%)
These are within the <=2% threshold product asked for. Full eval artifacts uploaded to s3://rwd-evals/mpt-x0/2026-03-15/ (manifest + per-task csv).

liam: +1 for AWQ as primary for serving. Operational asks: do a canary rollout (5% traffic -> 25% over 24h) with these auto-rollback triggers:
- latency > 1.5x baseline
- error rate spike > 3x baseline
- quality regression > 2% on monitored eval prompts

aj: Approved from infra/config side once PR merged and batch size default lowered. :thumbsup:

quant-ops: APPROVED — AWQ rollout OK under conditions:
1) calibration artifacts present (confirmed)
2) canary rollout policy created and annotated in the change (liam's plan)
3) eval results linked to monitoring dashboard and eval alert thresholds set
Tagging @maya to implement the change and post the canary plan URL. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks all. I'll merge PR after fixing nits, update serve_config (max_input=2048 + default batch=2), trigger calib jobs, and create the canary rollout change. Will post the canary change URL and monitoring dashboard link here when ready.

quant-ops: Please add a post-deploy smoke run (latency + correctness) to the canary checklist.

maya: Will do.

aj: FYI I left a small comment on PR about logging level for kv-cache errors — suggest warn not error to avoid noisy pages during canary.

maya: Noted, will change to warn. Thanks everyone!
